question: Points $P$ and $Q$ have position vectors $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$, respectively. Find the position vectors of the points dividing $PQ$ in the ratio $2:1$ (i) internally and (ii) externally.
explanation:
Step 1: Internal division
For internal division in the ratio $2:1$,
\(\vec{r}_1=\frac{2\vec{b}+\vec{a}}{3}\)
Substitution gives
\(\vec{r}_1=\frac{2(-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{3}=\frac{7}{3}\hat{j}+\frac{7}{3}\hat{k}\)
Step 2: External division
For external division in the ratio $2:1$,
\(\vec{r}_2=\frac{2\vec{b}-\vec{a}}{2-1}\)
Step 3: Simplification of the external position vector
\(\vec{r}_2=2(-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})=-4\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\)
Final Answer
Internal: $\frac{7}{3}\hat{j}+\frac{7}{3}\hat{k}$; external: $-4\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$.
